title: Faceting and Small Multiples
description: Trellis display architecture using repetitive sub-charts to compare distributions across high-dimensional segments.
conditions: Visualizing complex relationships conditioned on 1 or 2 categorical segment variables
Single plot becomes overcrowded and uninterpretable with multi-colored overlapping lines or points
recommended_methods: Small multiples grid (e.g. FacetGrid / trellis) sharing consistent x and y axis scales
One-variable wrap faceting (e.g. one panel per Region)
Two-variable matrix faceting (e.g. rows = Gender, columns = Age Cohort)
selection_rules: Keep axis scales FIXED across all panels to ensure honest cross-panel visual comparisons
Order panels logically by aggregate metric volume or alphabetical order
Limit total number of small multiple panels to <= 16 to avoid excessive cognitive overload
limitations: Fixed axis scales can flatten curves in low-volume panels (allow independent y-scales only if clearly annotated)
Requires larger canvas size in exported reports and presentations
